(************************************************************
* Reductions
************************************************************)

trait Reduction[\L\]
    getter reverse():Reduction[\L\] = ReversedReduction[\L\](self)
    empty(): L
    join(a: L, b: L): L
end

object ReversedReduction[\R\](r:Reduction[\R\]) extends Reduction[\R\]
  getter reverse():Reduction[\R\] = r
  getter asString():String = "ReversedReduction(" || r.asString || ")"
  empty():R = r.empty()
  join(x:R,y:R):R = r.join(y,x)
end

(** Invariants:
    join must be associative with identity empty
    unlift(lift(x)) = x
 **)
trait ActualReduction[\R,L\] extends Reduction[\L\]
    lift(r: R): L
    unlift(l:L): R
    (** If this reduction left-distributes over r, return a pair of
        reductions with the same lift and unlift **)
    leftDistribute(r: Reduction[\R\]): PossibleReductionPair[\R\] =
        distribute(r)
    (** If this reduction right-distributes over r, return a pair of
        reductions with the same lift and unlift **)
    rightDistribute(r: Reduction[\R\]): PossibleReductionPair[\R\] =
        distribute(r)
    (** If this reduction distributes over r, return a pair of
        reductions with the same lift and unlift **)
    (* a hack to avoid the error of overloaded methods *)
    distribute(r: Any): PossibleReductionPair[\R\] =
        NoReductionPair[\R\]
(*    distribute[\K\](r: ActualReduction[\R,K\]): PossibleReductionPair[\R\] =
        NoReductionPair[\R\]
*)
end

trait PossibleReductionPair[\R\] extends Condition[\PossibleReductionPair[\R\]\]
    comprises { NoReductionPair[\R\], SomeReductionPair[\R\] }
end

object NoReductionPair[\R\] extends PossibleReductionPair[\R\]
    getter holds(): Boolean = false
    cond[\G\](t:PossibleReductionPair[\R\]->G, e:()->G): G = e()
end

trait SomeReductionPair[\R\] extends PossibleReductionPair[\R\]
    getter holds(): Boolean = true
    getter outer(): Reduction[\R\]
    getter inner(): Reduction[\R\]
    cond[\G\](t:PossibleReductionPair[\R\]->G, e:()->G): G = t(self)
end

trait ReductionPair[\R,L\] extends SomeReductionPair[\L\]
    getter outer(): ActualReduction[\R,L\]
    getter inner(): ActualReduction[\R,L\]
....




trait SomeCommutativeReduction end

trait CommutativeReduction[\R\] extends { AssociativeReduction[\R\], SomeCommutativeReduction }
    getter reverse():CommutativeReduction[\R\] = self
end

(** Monoids don't require a special lift and unlift operation. **)
trait MonoidReduction[\R\] extends ActualReduction[\R,R\]
    lift(r:R): R = r
    unlift(r:R): R = r
end

trait CommutativeMonoidReduction[\R\] extends { MonoidReduction[\R\], SomeCommutativeReduction}
    getter reverse():CommutativeMonoidReduction[\R\] = self
end

trait ReductionWithZeroes[\R,L\] extends ActualReduction[\R,L\]
    isLeftZero(l:L): Boolean = isZero(l)
    isRightZero(l:L): Boolean = isZero(l)
    isZero(l:L): Boolean = false
end

trait BigOperator[\I,O,R,L\]
    getter reduction(): ActualReduction[\R,L\]
    getter body(): I->R
    getter unwrap(): R->O
end

object BigReduction[\R,L\](reduction:ActualReduction[\R,L\]) extends BigOperator[\R,R,R,L\]
    getter body(): R->R = fn x => x
    getter unwrap(): R->R = fn x => x
end

object Comprehension[\I,O,R,L\](unwrap: R->O, reduction: ActualReduction[\R,L\], body:I->R)
        extends BigOperator[\I,O,R,L\]
end

(** VoidReduction is usually done for effect, so we pretend that
    the completion performs the effects.  This rules out things
    distributing over void (that would change the number of effects in
    our program) but not void distributing over other things. **)
object VoidReduction extends { CommutativeMonoidReduction[\()\] }
    getter asString(): String = "VoidReduction"
    getter reverse(): Reduction[\()\] = VoidReduction
    empty(): () = ()
    join(a: (), b: ()): () = ()
end

__bigOperatorSugar[\(T,U),(T,U),(T,U),Maybe[\(T,U)\]\](BIG MAX_MAX[\T,U\](), g)


(** AndReduction and OrReduction take advantage of natural zeroes for early exit. **)
object AndReduction
        extends { CommutativeMonoidReduction[\Boolean\],
                  ReductionWithZeroes[\Boolean,Boolean\] }
    getter asString(): String = "AndReduction"
    empty(): Boolean = true
    join(a: Boolean, b: Boolean): Boolean = a AND b
    isZero(a:Boolean): Boolean = NOT a
end

opr BIG AND[\T\](): BigReduction[\Boolean,Boolean\] =
    BigReduction[\Boolean,Boolean\](AndReduction)

opr BIG AND[\T\](g: Generator[\Boolean\]): Boolean =
    __bigOperatorSugar[\Boolean,Boolean,Boolean,Boolean\](BIG AND[\T\](), g)

object OrReduction
        extends { CommutativeMonoidReduction[\Boolean\],
                  ReductionWithZeroes[\Boolean,Boolean\] }
    getter asString(): String = "OrReduction"
    empty(): Boolean = false
    join(a: Boolean, b: Boolean): Boolean = a OR b
    isZero(a:Boolean): Boolean = a
end

opr BIG OR[\T\](): BigReduction[\Boolean, Boolean\] =
    BigReduction[\Boolean,Boolean\](OrReduction)

opr BIG OR[\T\](g: Generator[\Boolean\]): Boolean =
    __bigOperatorSugar[\Boolean,Boolean,Boolean,Boolean\](BIG OR[\T\](), g)


(** Operator reductions on integers *)

(*
object BitXorReduction[\T extends Integral[\T\]\]
        extends { CommutativeMonoidReduction[\T\] }
    getter asString(): String = "BitXorReduction"
    empty(): T = 0
    join(a: T, b: T): T = a BITXOR b
end

opr BIG BITXOR[\T extends Integral[\T\]\](): BigReduction[\T, T\] =
    BigReduction[\T,T\](BitXorReduction)

opr BIG BITXOR[\T extends Integral[\T\]\](g: Generator[\T\]): T =
    __bigOperatorSugar[\T,T,T,T\](BIG BITXOR[\T\](), g)
*)

object BitXorReduction
        extends { CommutativeMonoidReduction[\ZZ32\] }
    getter asString(): String = "BitXorReduction"
    empty(): ZZ32 = 0
    join(a: ZZ32, b: ZZ32): ZZ32 = a BITXOR b
end

opr BIG BITXOR(): BigReduction[\ZZ32, ZZ32\] =
    BigReduction[\ZZ32,ZZ32\](BitXorReduction)

opr BIG BITXOR(g: Generator[\ZZ32\]): ZZ32 =
    __bigOperatorSugar[\ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32\](BIG BITXOR(), g)

(** A reduction performing String concatenation **)
object StringReduction extends MonoidReduction[\String\]
    getter asString(): String = "StringReduction"
    empty(): String = ""
    join(a:String, b:String): String = a || b
end

(** A reduction performing String concatenation with a space **)
object SpaceReduction extends MonoidReduction[\String\]
    getter asString(): String = "StringReduction"
    empty(): String = ""
    join(a:String, b:String): String = a ||| b
end

(** A reduction performing String concatenation with newline separation **)
object NewlineReduction extends AssociativeReduction[\String\]
    getter asString(): String = "NewlineReduction"
    simpleJoin(a:String, b:String): String = a // b
end

(** This operator performs string concatenation, first converting
    its inputs (of type Any) to String if necessary. **)
opr BIG ||(): Comprehension[\Any,String,String,String\] =
    Comprehension[\Any,String,String,String\](
        identity[\String\],StringReduction,fn (x:Any)=> "" x)

opr BIG ||[\T\](g: Generator[\T\]): String =
    __bigOperatorSugar[\Any,String,String,String\](BIG ||(), g.map[\Any\](identity[\Any\]))

(** This operator performs string concatenation, first converting
    its inputs (of type Any) to String if necessary, and separating
    non-empty components by a space. **)
opr BIG |||(): Comprehension[\Any,String,String,String\] =
    Comprehension[\Any,String,String,String\](
        identity[\String\],SpaceReduction,fn (x:Any)=> "" x)

opr BIG |||[\T\](g: Generator[\T\]): String =
    __bigOperatorSugar[\Any,String,String,String\](BIG |||(), g.map[\Any\](identity[\Any\]))

(** This operator performs string concatenation with newline
    separation, first converting its inputs (of type Any) to String if
    necessary. **)
opr BIG //(): Comprehension[\Any,String,String,Maybe[\String\]\] =
    Comprehension[\Any,String,String,Maybe[\String\]\](
        fn x => x,NewlineReduction,fn (x:Any)=> "" x)

opr BIG //[\T\](g: Generator[\T\]): String =
    __bigOperatorSugar[\Any,String,String,Maybe[\String\]\](BIG //(), g.map[\Any\](identity[\Any\]))

(** A %MapReduceReduction% takes an associative binary function %j% on
    arguments of type %R%, and the identity of that function %z%, and
    returns the corresponding reduction. **)
object MapReduceReduction[\R\](j:(R,R)->R, z:R) extends MonoidReduction[\R\]
    getter asString(): String = "mapReduceReduction"
    empty(): R = z
    join(a:R, b:R): R = (j)(a,b)
end

(** A %MIMapReduceReduction% takes an associative binary function %j% on
    arguments of type %R%, and the identity of that function %z%, and
    returns the corresponding reduction. **)
object MIMapReduceReduction[\R\](j:(Any,Any)->R, z:R) extends MonoidReduction[\Any\]
    getter asString():String="MIMapReduceReduction from embiggen"
    empty(): R = z
    join(a:Any, b:Any): R = (j)(a,b)
end

(** %embiggen% takes a type %T% and an operation (either an operator
    %OP% or binary function %f% on type %T%), along with the identity
    %z% of the operation, and returns a function suitable as the right-hand
    side of the definition of the corresponding BIG operator. **)
(*
embiggen[\T,opr OP\](z:Any, g:(Reduction[\Any\],T->Any) -> Any) : T =
    g(MIOprReduction[\T,OP\](z), fn (x) => x)
*)
embiggen[\T\](j:(Any,Any)->T, z:T) : Comprehension[\T,T,Any,Any\] =
    Comprehension[\T,T,Any,Any\](fn (x) => x, MIMapReduceReduction[\T\](j,z), fn (x) => x)

(** Helpers for maps and cross products of generators.  These can be
    quite a bit more sophisticated (for example, we can hoist maps
    outwards if we think that'd be useful), but let's get this much
    working first. *)
trait SomeMappedGenerator[\F\] extends Generator[\F\] end

trait MappedGenerator[\E,F\] extends SomeMappedGenerator[\F\]
    getter g(): Generator[\E\]
    getter f(): E -> F
    getter asString(): String = "mapped(" (self asif Generator[\F\]).asString ")"
    getter reverse(): SimpleMappedGenerator[\E,F\] = SimpleMappedGenerator[\E,F\](self.g.reverse, self.f)

(** The following top-level functions are used as glue in the
    desugaring of generated expressions (comprehensions, BIG
    operators, and loops).  They exist at the top level in part to
    work around shortcomings in the ablity of the Fortress interpreter
    to check types dynamically for anything except top-level
    non-overloaded function calls. **)
__generate[\E,R\](g:Generator[\E\], r: Reduction[\R\], b:E->R): R =
    g.generate[\R\](r,b)

__nest[\E1,E2\](g:Generator[\E1\], f:E1->Generator[\E2\]):Generator[\E2\] =
    g.nest[\E2\](f)

__singleton[\E\](body:E): Generator[\E\] = Just[\E\](body)

__loop[\E\](g:Generator[\E\], body:E->()): () = g.loop(body)

__cond[\E,R\](c:Condition[\E\], t:E->R, e:()->R): R = c.cond[\R\](t,e)
__cond[\E\](c:Condition[\E\], t:E->()): () = c.cond[\()\](t, fn () => ())

(** Used in desugaring binding %while% **)
__whileCond[\E\](c:Condition[\E\], b:E->()): Boolean =
    c.cond[\Boolean\](fn (e): Boolean => do b(e); true end, fn ():Boolean => false)

(** Unlike the user-visible dotted map method, this method is used for
    the internals of comprehension desugaring [except that at present
    it is not actually in use, but we're planning to use it].  As a
    result we know that its result will immediately be consumed, and
    we should *not* create an intermediate collection if we're passed
    a collection. **)
__map[\E,R\](g:Generator[\E\], f:E->R): Generator[\R\] =
    typecase g of
        g':SomeMappedGenerator[\E\] => g'.map[\R\](f)
        g':SequentialGenerator[\E\] => SimpleMappedSeqGenerator[\E,R\](g',f)
        else => SimpleMappedGenerator[\E,R\](g,f)
    end

(** Unlike the user-visible dotted filter method, but like the __map
    method, this method is intended for use in the internals of
    comprehension desugaring.  Again its result will immediately be
    consumed, and we do not create an intermediate collection but
    perform the filtering lazily on demand. **)
__filter[\E\](g:Generator[\E\], p:E->Condition[\()\]): Generator[\E\] =
do
    typecase g of
        g':SomeGenerator2 => g'.filter(p)
        g':FilterGenerator[\E\] => g'.filter(p)
        g':SequentialGenerator[\E\] => SimpleSeqFilterGenerator[\E\](g',p)
        else => SimpleFilterGenerator[\E\](g,p)
    end
end

(** Invariants:
    join must be associative with identity empty
    unlift(lift(x)) = x
 **)
trait ActualReduction[\R,L\] extends Reduction[\L\]
    abstract empty(): L
    abstract join(a: L, b: L): L
    abstract lift(r:R): L
    abstract unlift(l:L): R
    (** If this reduction left-distributes over r, return a pair of
        reductions with the same lift and unlift **)
    leftDistribute(r: Reduction[\R\]): Maybe[\(Reduction[\R\],Reduction[\R\])\]
    (** If this reduction right-distributes over r, return a pair of
        reductions with the same lift and unlift **)
    rightDistribute(r: Reduction[\R\]): Maybe[\(Reduction[\R\],Reduction[\R\])\]
    (** If this reduction distributes over r, return a pair of
        reductions with the same lift and unlift **)
    distribute(r: Reduction[\R\]): Maybe[\(Reduction[\R\],Reduction[\R\])\]
end

trait PossibleReductionPair[\R\] extends Condition[\PossibleReductionPair[\R\]\]
    comprises { NoReductionPair[\R\], SomeReductionPair[\R\] }
end

object NoReductionPair[\R\] extends PossibleReductionPair[\R\]
    getter holds(): Boolean
    cond[\G\](t:PossibleReductionPair[\R\]->G, e:()->G): G
end

trait SomeReductionPair[\R\] extends PossibleReductionPair[\R\]
    getter holds(): Boolean
    abstract getter outer(): Reduction[\R\]
    abstract getter inner(): Reduction[\R\]
    cond[\G\](t:PossibleReductionPair[\R\]->G, e:()->G): G
end

trait ReductionPair[\R,L\] extends SomeReductionPair[\R\]
    abstract getter outer(): ActualReduction[\R,L\]
    abstract getter inner(): ActualReduction[\R,L\]
end

(** The usual lifting to Maybe for identity-less operators **)
trait AssociativeReduction[\R\] extends ActualReduction[\R,Maybe[\R\]\]
    empty(): Nothing[\R\]
    join(a: Maybe[\R\], b: Maybe[\R\]): Maybe[\R\]
    abstract simpleJoin(a:R, b:R): R
    lift(r:R): Maybe[\R\]
    unlift(r:Maybe[\R\]): R
end

trait SomeCommutativeReduction end (* mark for commutative *)

trait DistributesOver[\E\] end (* marking for distributivity *)

trait CommutativeReduction[\R\] extends {AssociativeReduction[\R\], SomeCommutativeReduction} end

(** Monoids don't require a special lift and unlift operation. **)
trait MonoidReduction[\R\] extends ActualReduction[\R,R\]
    lift(r:R): R
    unlift(r:R): R
end

trait CommutativeMonoidReduction[\R\] extends {MonoidReduction[\R\], SomeCommutativeReduction} end

## The row template

A row is one line of eight cells, `| # | claim | status | class | spec citation | reproducer | found by | notes / workaround |`, at most 1,200 characters, in the table of its topic section, in number order. A pipe inside a cell is written `\|`. (POSITIONS, "The gap ledger's form"; the proposal behind it is `explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md`, section 4.)

- **#**: the row's number, the next free one when it is added; never reused, renumbered or given to another row. 148 is vacant.
- **claim**: at most 300 characters, whose first 150 name the defect or the capability: what fails or what holds, and where.
- **status**: exactly one word of seven, with no second status and nothing in brackets:
  - `POSITIVE-VERIFIED`: it works; it ran and its output is recorded.
  - `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`: the specification settles it and the reproducer confirms it. A row with one half fixed stays `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`, and its notes say which half is fixed.
  - `NEGATIVE-BOUNDED`: the failure reproduces; the mechanisms tried are named and are not exhaustive.
  - `CONTESTED`: unsettled; the notes say why.
  - `RETIRED`: a source's claim falsified here, kept so that it is not derived again.
  - `FIXED`: closed by a landed commit (`ledger.py close`): the claim's first sentence, the test as reproducer, notes `fixed HASH; full text: history, row N`.
  - `DUPLICATE`: a pointer (`ledger.py duplicate`), notes `duplicate of row M; full text: history, row N`.
- **class**: `kind (area)`; `—` only for `POSITIVE-VERIFIED` and `RETIRED`. The kind is one of `implementation gap`, `library gap vs spec`, `library bug`, `design limit`, `deliberate`, `typesetter`, `packaging`; the area one of `parser`, `walk`, `checker`, `codegen`, `runtime`, `library`, `prelude`, `specification`, `tests`, `tools`.
- **spec citation**: the `.tex` file and the section heading in quotes, as `basic/operators/juxtameaning.tex`, "Juxtaposition"; a line number only against `Specification-1.0-frozen/`; `silent` where the specification does not say.
- **reproducer**: one test (its name, or its path under the test folders; an `XXX` test while it is an expected failure) or one probe path from the repository root, at most 200 characters; `none` when nothing in the tree reproduces it, with the command and its output, or the probe's old path, in the notes.
- **found by**: the stream that found it (`climb batch 8 rung I`, `run-c3`, `apl rung 2`), at most 60 characters; no date and no role.
- **notes / workaround**: at most 700 characters: `siblings: N, M` first if there are any; the mechanism, with file:line and the commit it was true at; the workaround; for a closed row, `fixed HASH`.

A path under `explorations/` that is no longer in the tree is read from history: `git show $(git log -1 --diff-filter=D --format=%h -- PATH)^:PATH`.

import Set.{...}
import Map.{...}
export Executable

object MyCat extends AssociativeReduction[\String\]
    getter asString(): String = "MyCat"
    simpleJoin(a:String, b:String): String = a || "-" || b
end

minOf[\T extends StandardMin[\T\]\](g: Generator[\T\]): T = BIG MIN[x <- g] x

run(): () = do
    println("strmin " (BIG MIN[i <- 0#3] ("x" i)))
    println("strmax " (BIG MAX[i <- 0#3] ("x" i)))
    println("rrmax " (BIG MAX[i <- 0#4] (0.5 i)))
    println("filtermin " (BIG MIN[i <- 0#10, i > 3] i))
    println("twogen " (BIG MAX[i <- 0#3, j <- 0#3] (i + j)))
    println("nested " (BIG MAX[i <- 0#3] (SUM[j <- 0#3] (i + j))))
    println("nestedmin " (BIG MIN[i <- 0#3] (BIG MAX[j <- 0#3] (i + j))))
    println("minmaxw " (BIG MINMAX[\ZZ32\][i <- 0#4] i))
    println("interw " (BIG INTERSECTION[\ZZ32\][i <- 0#3] {[\ZZ32\] i, 1}))
    println("unionw " (BIG UNION[\ZZ32\][i <- 0#3] {[\ZZ32\] i}))
    println("listmin " (BIG MIN <|[\ZZ32\] 4, 2, 7 |>))
    println("listmaxs " (BIG MAX[\String\][s <- <|[\String\] "a", "c", "b" |>] s))
    println("nl " (BIG //[i <- 0#2] i))
    println("mycat " MyCat.unlift((0#3).generate[\Maybe[\String\]\](MyCat, fn i => MyCat.lift("" i))))
    println("minOf " minOf(3#4))
    println("minOfW " minOf[\ZZ32\](3#4))
    println("setcomp " {i | i <- 0#3})
    println("listcomp " <| 2 i | i <- 0#3 |>)
    println("mapcomp " {i |-> 10 i | i <- 0#3})
    try
      r = BIG MIN[i <- 0#0] i
      println("emptymin returned " r)
    catch x EmptyReduction => println("emptymin EmptyReduction")
    end
    try
      r = BIG //[i <- 0#0] i
      println("emptynl returned " r)
    catch x EmptyReduction => println("emptynl EmptyReduction")
    end
    try
      r = BIG MINMAX[i <- 0#0] i
      println("emptyminmax returned " r)
    catch x EmptyReduction => println("emptyminmax EmptyReduction")
    end
    println("DONE")
  end

end
EOF
cat > SkAnyRed.fss <<'EOF'
component SkAnyRed
export Executable

object OldCat extends AssociativeReduction[\String\]
    getter asString(): String = "OldCat"
    simpleJoin(a:Any, b:Any): Any = "" a "-" b
end

run(): () = do
    println("oldcat " OldCat.unlift((0#3).generate[\AnyMaybe\](OldCat, fn i => OldCat.lift("" i))))
    println("DONE")
  end

end
EOF

  "Under `walk`, a type parameter whose bound mentions itself" FACTS.md:147, Landed semantics  [2306 bytes]

== explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md, ## Landed semantics

FACTS.md:147
- **Under `walk`, a type parameter whose bound mentions itself and that nothing at a call fixes is left open, an object inherits no declaration that a trait's `override` declaration overrides on every path, and an object expression is checked under the Meet Rule for Functional Methods** (`compile-ladder/rung-walk-open-param/REPORT.md`; row 424's F-bounded half and rows 614 and 618 fixed; rows 645 to 649 opened, row 473's open half given an expected failure). `EvaluatorBase.instanceOf` gives such a parameter `BottomType.OPEN` (`interpreter/evaluator/EvaluatorBase.java:184-194`). The open type is below every type, and every value matches it where walk checks a value against a type: `typeMatch`, `as`, `asif`, a `typecase` clause and a typed local. So a reduction that writes no static argument runs on its elements' types, and `ilkName` prints such an instance as `BoxU[\OPEN\]`. Only the open type itself admits every value: a tuple, arrow or generic type that holds it admits no more than at `BottomType`, so `(Int, Int)` is not below `(OPEN, OPEN)` at dispatch (row 473). Being below every type, a declaration whose parameter type is the open type is the most specific one that applies, so it is chosen over the others for every argument: in a `Holder[\OPEN\]`, `take(x: T)` runs for `3` beside `take(x: ZZ32)`, and for `"s"`, which no declaration admitted at `BottomType`. A big operator's plain-bounded static parameters stay at `BottomType` (D2). `Constructor.overriddenInTraits` reads `override` per type, as the load check does (row 615). `BuildEnvironments.finishObjectTrait` runs `FunctionalMethodMeets` on an object expression without static parameters; one in a generic function takes the function's static parameters and is not checked, as a generic object is not (row 647). Gated by `tests/UnwrittenReductionWalk.fss`, `InferUnfixedFBoundedWalk.fss`, `OverrideInTraitWalk.fss` and `FunctionalMethodMeetObjectExpressionWalk.fss`; the residues by `XXXUnwrittenEmptyFloatSumWalk.fss`, `XXXUnwrittenBigMinMaxWalk.fss`, `XXXComprehensionTypedBindingWalk.fss` and `XXXFunctionalMethodMeetGenericProviderWalk.fss`; an object below a trait whose abstract `override` declaration overrides a concrete one inherits only the abstract one, which walk does not refuse at load (row 649).

# Climb batch 12: the review's reasons

The record's header names this note; the coordinator diffs the record and the generator against `6067ccb25` and folds what it accepts. Section and question numbers are the record's. The generator's three checks pass on the reviewed files: `lists12.py` finds every briefing key at exactly one place, `gen12.py` writes the block (347 lines), and `check12.js` reports 42 checks ok and 0 problems on the scratch splice; the tracked script still carries batch 11's block, which the coordinator's step 5 replaces (`check12.js --write`).

## 1. Changes made, one reason each

1. **Header.** The review sentence, in the form batch 11's record carries (`coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-11.md:1`): what reviewed the draft, on what pre-approval, against which `main`, and that `main`'s one commit since the draft's base is the draft (`git log ae93dd1ae..HEAD`: `6067ccb25`).

2. **Row 644's repair makes a sentence of Appendix I false, and rung C did not know it.** C's "Specification" paragraph said "Row 644: none; the chapter already names an operator application." The chapter does: the sentence after its list of contexts says the expected type is used whether the call is written by juxtaposition, "or as a method invocation or an operator application" (`Specification/basic/inference.tex:143-145`). But rung E's Appendix I entry "The contexts that give a call an expected type" says at `Specification/appendices/changes.tex:2047-2051`: "Nor does it give one to an operator repeated between three or more operands that no multifix declaration accepts, as p ⊕ q ⊕ r, though the outer of the binary applications (p ⊕ q) ⊕ r that it stands for is an operator application, which the sentence after the list gives the expected type (row 644)." A grep of `Specification/` for `row~644` finds it. The manual asks that a rung be briefed with every Appendix I Effect its change makes false (`climb-batch-workflow.md`, "Preparing a batch record"; batch 9's one blocking finding was such a miss). So C amends that sentence in the S1 form whatever Q48's answer, and under Q48 the entry's two label-body sentences (`:1998-2001`, `:2043-2046`) too. Changed: section 1's line for C; C's row 644 line and "Specification" paragraph; C's blurb; in `lists12.py`, the reason beside the entry's key, and the key added to `C_CHECKS` (12 checks now), since the skeptic compares the ame

3. **The inference chapter's line numbers.** The draft cited the list of contexts as `:128-141` and the "not yet described" item as `:262-264`. On this tree the list runs `:128-142` (its last clause, the `typecase` union, ends at `:142`), the sentence that gives an operator application the type is `:143-145`, and the item naming "an argument of another call, the body of a `for` loop or the body of a `label` expression" is `:266-268`; `:262-265` is the item on converting an argument whose parameter type mentions a static parameter. PLAN item 48 has `:266-268`. A worker sent to `:262-264` would have edited the wrong item. The entry's bounds are `:1984-2082` (the next `\subsection` is `:2083`), and its label sentences `:1998-2001` and `:2043-2046`, not `:2000` and `:2044-2046`. Changed in Q48 ("On file", "The specification"), rung C (row 644, "Specification") and the two `inference.tex` reasons of `lists12.py`.

4. **G's test asserted `BIG MINMAX`'s unwritten form as passing before, and probe P2 ran on the shadow only.** G's test listed `BIG MINMAX` among the operators whose unwritten clause form it asserts, "passes before and after". runRanges(x: Indexed[\Boolean,ZZ32\]): List[\CompactFullRange[\ZZ32\]\] =
  (BIG BOXPLUS[i <- 0 # |x|] (if x[i] then RangeSet(0, <|[\CompactFullRange[\ZZ32\]\] i:i |>, 0) else SingleRange(1))).ranges

opr BIG BOXPLUS[\T\](): BigReduction[\RunRanges, RunRanges\] =
   embiggen[\RunRanges\](fn(a,b) => a BOXPLUS b, SingleRange(0))

trait RunRanges comprises { SingleRange, RangeSet }
  getter ranges(): List[\CompactFullRange[\ZZ32\]\]
  opr BOXPLUS(self, x: RunRanges): RunRanges
end

object SingleRange(n: ZZ32) extends RunRanges
  getter ranges() = <|[\CompactFullRange[\ZZ32\]\] |>
  opr BOXPLUS(self, other: SingleRange) = SingleRange(n + other.n)
  opr BOXPLUS(self, other: RangeSet) = RangeSet(n + other.left, other.ranges, other.right)
end

object RangeSet(left: ZZ32, ranges: List[\CompactFullRange[\ZZ32\]\], right: ZZ32) extends RunRanges
  opr BOXPLUS(self, other: SingleRange) = RangeSet(left, ranges, right + other.n)
  opr BOXPLUS(self, other: RangeSet) =
    if right + other.left >= 2 then
      RangeSet(left, ranges || other.ranges, other.right)
    else
      (ps, p) = ranges.extractRight.get
      (q, qs) = other.ranges.extractLeft.get
      RangeSet(left, ps || <| p.lower:q.upper |> || qs, other.right)
    end
end

geometricMean(xs: List[\RR64\]): RR64 = (PROD xs)^(1.0/(|xs|))

opr UNIONCAT[\T,U\](a: Map[\T, List[\U\]\], b: Map[\T, List[\U\]\]): Map[\T, List[\U\]\] =
  a.union(fn(k,x,y) => x || y, b)

opr BIG UNIONCAT[\T,U\](): BigReduction[\Map[\T, List[\U\]\],Map[\T, List[\U\]\]\] =
  embiggen[\Map[\T, List[\U\]\]\](fn(a,b) => a UNIONCAT b, {[\T,List[\U\]\]})

opr UNIONPLUS[\T\](a: Map[\T, ZZ32\], b: Map[\T, ZZ32\]): Map[\T, ZZ32\] =
  a.union(fn(k,x,y) => x + y, b)

opr BIG UNIONPLUS[\T\](): BigReduction[\Map[\T, ZZ32\],Map[\T, ZZ32\]\] =
  embiggen[\Map[\T, ZZ32\]\](fn(a,b) => a UNIONPLUS b, {[\T,ZZ32\]})

end

relation[\T\](domain: Set[\T\], f: T -> Set[\T\]): Relation[\T\] =
  Relation[\T\] {[\T,Set[\T\]\] key |-> f(key) | key <- domain }

relation[\T\](rel: Map[\T,Set[\T\]\]): Relation[\T\] =
  Relation[\T\] {[\T,Set[\T\]\] key |-> vals | (key, vals) <- rel, NOT vals.isEmpty }

relation[\T\](pairs: Generator[\(T,T)\]): Relation[\T\] =
  BIG RELATION[\T\][p <- pairs] p

opr BIG RELATION[\T\](): Comprehension[\(T,T), Relation[\T\], Map[\T,Set[\T\]\], Map[\T,Set[\T\]\]\] =
  Comprehension[\(T,T), Relation[\T\], Map[\T,Set[\T\]\], Map[\T,Set[\T\]\]\](
    Relation[\T\],
    RelationReduction[\T\],
    fn(k:T,v:T):Map[\T,Set[\T\]\] => {[\T,Set[\T\]\] k |-> {[\T\] v } })

opr BIG RELATION[\T\](g: Generator[\(T,T)\]):Relation[\T\] =
  __bigOperatorSugar[\(T,T),Relation[\T\],Map[\T,Set[\T\]\],Map[\T,Set[\T\]\]\](BIG RELATION[\T\](), g)

object RelationReduction[\T\] extends CommutativeMonoidReduction[\Map[\T,Set[\T\]\]\]
  getter asString():String = "Relation reduction"
  empty():Map[\T,Set[\T\]\] = {[\T,Set[\T\]\]}
  join(left: Map[\T,Set[\T\]\], right: Map[\T,Set[\T\]\]):Map[\T,Set[\T\]\] =
    relationUnion(left, right)
end

(* Helpers *)

transitiveLoop[\T\](accum:Map[\T,Set[\T\]\], working:Map[\T,Set[\T\]\]):Map[\T,Set[\T\]\] =
  if working.isEmpty then accum else
    generated = relationCompose[\T\](working, accum)
    newAccum = relationUnion[\T\](accum, generated)
    newWorking = relationDifference[\T\](newAccum, accum)
    transitiveLoop[\T\](newAccum, newWorking)
  end

## The model program

MicroGPT runs only under walk, by hand, never in the gate. Check the model when your brief asks for it: run your tree's `explorations/coordinator/tools/mg-run.sh <work-dir> <label> [threads]`. `<work-dir>` is a folder under your tree's `tmp/`, and `threads` sets `FORTRESS_THREADS`, 1 by default. The script runs the quick pair at once, `MicroGptFlatQuick.fss` and `MicroGptAplQuick.fss`: two forward and backward passes each, against the reference values, in about 56 s for both. Each starts from an empty private cache and writes `<work-dir>/<name>.txt`. Read its `VERDICT:` line and its last line, `rc=`.

- Add the word `full` only if your brief asks for it. It runs the full pair, `MicroGptFlatCheck.fss` and `MicroGptAplCheck.fss`, with 40 checks each and a 90-minute timeout.
- If you change a line of the model, put the change in your report as a diff.

content.content:
- Reason: the paper is the type group's latest word on the rule.

**A type parameter whose bound names itself, under walk**

- Original: walk gave such a parameter the empty type `Bottom` where a call did not fix it, as `SUM`'s `T extends AdditiveGroup[\T\]` in `SUM[i <- 1#100] i`. The reduction then refused its first element. The POPL 2019 paper's rule has no bound to give: such a bound is not a type until the parameter is known.
- Resolution: walk leaves the parameter open. Wherever walk checks a value against the open parameter, every value passes, so the reduction runs on the types of its elements. An empty reduction gives `ZZ32`'s identity, whatever the type of its elements (ledger row 645). `BIG MINMAX` still stops (ledger row 473). A printed type shows the open parameter as `OPEN`: `BoxU[\OPEN\]` for an object `BoxU[\T\]`. The checker still refuses the call (ledger row 425).
- Reason: walk has no static types, so it cannot take the element type from the static type of the reduced expression, as the specification's desugaring does (`Specification/basic/expressions/reductions.tex`). An open parameter refuses no element.

## The curator's decisions on the library

- Scalar ranges are over `ZZ32` only. A range over another integer type is a static error, and walk stops when it builds one. Write a wider counter as a `ZZ32` loop that widens its index.
- `ZZ32` and numerals convert into `RR64` implicitly. `ZZ64` converts into `RR64` only explicitly, by `asFloat`.
- For arithmetic that wraps on overflow, use the wrapping operators ∔ `DOTPLUS`, ∸ `DOTMINUS` and ⨰ `DOTTIMES`. Parenthesise every such expression fully, because their precedence is stated only among themselves.
- `SUM` and `PROD` are generic over `AdditiveGroup` and `MultiplicativeRing`. If nothing at the call fixes the element type, write it: `SUM[\ZZ32\][j <- 0#n] f(j)`. The checker refuses a call without it (ledger row 425). Walk runs such a call, but an empty one gives `ZZ32`'s identity (ledger row 645), and `BIG MINMAX` stops (ledger row 473).
- An array's `fill` takes a value, and its `tabulate` a function of the index: `array[\ZZ32\](4).fill(0)`, `array[\ZZ32\](4).tabulate(fn (i:ZZ32):ZZ32 => 10 i)`. The factories that take a function are `tabulatedArray1` to `tabulatedArray3` and `tabulatedVector`.

content.content:
# The specification

Three folders hold the team's specification:

- `Specification/` is the team's text, as the revival revises it. It says what the language means, except where a decision of the curator says otherwise.
- `Specification-1.0-frozen/` is the unrevised copy. Cite it as "the Working Draft of February 2011". Only `fortress.1.0.pdf` in it is the 1.0 release. Leave this copy unchanged.
- `Documentation/Specification/` is the team's later restart, which they did not finish. If its Types chapter, `Documentation/Specification/Prose/Language/types.tick`, covers a topic, cite it beside `Specification/` as the designers' later word.

Appendix I, `Specification/appendices/changes.tex`, records the changes to the text. Its revival section has one entry for each change that the revival made.

A draft build prints the team's `\note{}` boxes, and a release build hides them. Many say that a feature was not built, for example "Reduction variables are not yet supported." Before you record a missing feature as a gap, grep the notes of its chapter: `grep -n '\\note{' Specification/<file>.tex`.

The api listings of the library part are generated from the library's `.fsi` files when the specification is built (`Specification/library/apis/`, not in the tree). A listing shows the library itself, so it cannot justify a change of the library. Cite the `.fsi` file.

## Weighing the sources

The type group is the part of the team that built the type checker and the compiler, from 2010 to 2012. Where their late positions disagree with the specification's earlier text, the curator gives the late positions more weight. These positions are:

- the exclusion rule;
- compiled code specialised to each instantiation of a generic, which they kept;
- the compiled number tower, which they flattened in 2011;
- the 2012 write-up on the Return Type Rule (`Papers/Types/journal/`);
- the POPL 2019 paper on symmetric multiple dispatch (`research/extracts/ParkPOPL2019-extract.md`).

When your report describes the team's sources on a question (`exploring.md`), say which of them is one of these positions.

If a conflict or a decision not taken needs the designers' reason for a rule, print the row of its design area. WORD is a word of the area, such as `coercion`, `juxtaposition`, `dispatch` or `Arrays`. A word can match several rows, each about 1 to 2 KB.

    explorations/coordinator/tools/facts-extract.sh 'map:design-intent-sources.md#The map, by design area@WORD'

Then open the sources that the row names. Among them are the `\note{}` boxes and the team's written rationale in the Internal Document appendix: `Specification/appendices/FAQ.tex` and `future.tex`.

## Changing the text: the revision form

Every change of the text has the four parts below, so that no disagreement between the text and an implementation stays hidden.

1. An entry in the revival section of Appendix I: a `\subsection` with a `\seclabel`. The entry gives:
   - the affected sections, the change, its rationale and its effect. The effect names each departure: each way in which walk or the compiled path does not do what the new text says, with its ledger row.
   - the original text, quoted with its path and line in `Specification-1.0-frozen/`;
   - what a reversal to the alternative not taken would need;
   - the decision of the curator that it follows (its POSITIONS entry), or the reason that your brief gives.

   For the form, print one entry, about 2 KB: `explorations/coordinator/tools/facts-extract.sh 'doc:Specification/appendices/changes.tex#choice of a coercion'`.

2. At each changed passage, a callout that prints in every build, unlike a `\note`:

       \revision{<label>}{<what changed, in a sentence or two>}

   `<label>` is the `\seclabel` of the entry. `Specification/fortress/fortress.tex` defines `\revision`.

3. The front matter's one paragraph on the revision, in `Specification/fortress/preamble.tex`. If your change makes it false, correct it.

4. The full reasoning, in `decision-record.md` in the folder of your work under `explorations/`: each changed passage, the original and the new text, the reason, and the way back. For the form, print one passage of an earlier record, about 4 KB: `explorations/coordinator/tools/facts-extract.sh 'doc:explorations/compile-ladder/rung-spec-route-a/decision-record.md#3.3'`.

If the revision refuses an example, keep the example in the text, marked "Not allowed", as the specification itself does. If your change contradicts a calculus of Appendix A, keep the calculus's rules and soundness claims. Add a callout to it that says what it predates.

Check each changed sentence of `Specification/` or `Documentation/` against the curator's decisions. If it says what walk or the compiled path does, run a program that shows it.

## Building it

To check your LaTeX, build the specification in a built tree, after the setup lines. It takes about 90 s, so start it detached (`session.md`, "Long commands"):

    nohup bash -c '( cd Specification/fortress && ./ant genSource && ./ant tex ) > tmp/spec.txt 2>&1; echo EXIT=$? >> tmp/spec.txt' >/dev/null 2>&1 &

- Both commands must end in `BUILD SUCCESSFUL`, and `grep -c 'Reference .* undefined\|multiply defined\|Undefined control sequence' Specification/fortress/fortress.log` must print 0.
- If `pdflatex` is missing, install the packages of the `PKGS` line of `explorations/experiment/setup.sh` with `apt-get update -qq && apt-get install -y`.
- The build writes only ignored files, its log among them, which can reach 400 MB. Remove them afterwards: `git clean -fXq -- Specification`.
- Update `Specification/fortress.pdf` only if your brief asks for it: copy `Specification/fortress/fortress.pdf` over it.

## When the text and an implementation disagree

- If a decision of the curator says which side is correct, the other side is wrong. If the wrong side is in your area, change it to agree. If not, record the departure as `tests-writing.md`, "How a defect is recorded", says.
- If no decision says so, the disagreement is a conflict. Switch to exploring (`exploring.md`).
- If the passage has an Appendix I entry, name the departure or the conflict in the entry's effect, with its ledger row. Then the text claims no more than holds.

## Citing it

- If your change renames or removes a section that a test names, update that citation in the same commit.
- Inside the text, cite a section with `\secref{label}`.

component UnwrittenBigMinMaxWalk
export Executable

(* BIG MINMAX with a generator clause list and no static argument answers the least and the greatest of its elements under walk. *)

run(): () = do
    (lo, hi) = BIG MINMAX[i <- 0#4] i
    assert(lo, 0, "BIG MINMAX with no static argument over 0#4 answers 0 as its least element (reductions.tex, section \"Summations and Other Reduction Expressions\")")
    assert(hi, 3, "BIG MINMAX with no static argument over 0#4 answers 3 as its greatest element (reductions.tex, section \"Summations and Other Reduction Expressions\")")
    println("PASS")
  end

end
\end{Fortress}
Here \VAR{R} is the result type of the operator, and \VAR{g} corresponds to
the method %generate[\R0\]
\EXP{\VAR{generate}\llbracket{}R_{0}\rrbracket}
of the trait %Generator[\T\]
\EXP{\TYP{Generator}\llbracket{}T\rrbracket}:
it is a function that takes a reduction (of type %Reduction[\R0\]
\EXP{\TYP{Reduction}\llbracket{}R_{0}\rrbracket})
and a body (of type \EXP{T\rightarrow{}R_{0}})
and returns a value of type \EXP{R_{0}} by running body on each
generated element and combining them using the reduction.
When a generator clause
list is provided, generator clauses produce values and bind the values to the
identifiers that are used in the subexpression.  Each iteration of the
body expression is assumed to be evaluated in a separate implicit
thread as described in \secref{generators}.  The resulting values are
combined together using \emph{Op}
\label{redexpr-redvar}
as with reduction variables (see \secref{reduction-vars}).
The value of a reduction expression is this combined value.
When no generator clause list is provided, the body is taken to be an
object of type \TYP{Generator} and the elements it generates are
combined.  Thus, the reduction expression \EXP{\sum a} is equivalent
to \EXP{\sum\limits_{x\leftarrow{}a}\mskip 4mu plus 4mu{x}}.

content.content:
component NotationGenericBigSum
export Executable

object D(v:RR64, d:RR64) extends AdditiveGroup[\D\]
  getter zero():D = D(0.0,0.0)
  opr +(self, y:D):D = D(v+y.v, d+y.d)
end

object AddReduction[\T extends AdditiveGroup[\T\]\] extends CommutativeReduction[\T\]
  simpleJoin(x:Any,y:Any):Any = do
    x':T = cast[\T\](x)
    y':T = cast[\T\](y)
    x'+y'
  end
end

(* Identity-less reduction permits a generic big SUM without requiring a
   run-time witness solely to obtain zero. *)
opr SUM[\T extends AdditiveGroup[\T\]\](): Comprehension[\T,T,T,AnyMaybe\] =
  Comprehension[\T,T,T,AnyMaybe\](fn (x:T) => x, AddReduction[\T\], fn (x:T) => x)

run():() = do
  s:D = SUM[\D\][i <- 1#4] D(1.0 i, 1.0)
  println(s.v)
  println(s.d)
end
end

(* The generator, condition, reduction and generator-of-generators declarations whose static arguments and declared types the compiled checker refused, called under walk with the values they answer. *)
component GeneratorDeclarations
import List.{...}
import Generator2.{...}
export Executable

inOrder[\E\](g: Generator[\E\]): String = do
    s: String := ""
    for x <- seq(g) do s := s || x || "," end
    s
end

fusedMax(gg: Generator[\Generator[\ZZ32\]\]): ZZ32 =
    __bigOperator2[\ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32,Maybe[\ZZ32\],ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32,Generator[\ZZ32\]\](
        BIG MAX[\ZZ32\](), SUM[\ZZ32\](), gg, fn (x: ZZ32): ZZ32 => x)

naiveMax(gg: Generator[\Generator[\ZZ32\]\]): ZZ32 = do
    switchDispatching(false)
    r = fusedMax(gg)
    switchDispatching(true)
    r
end

run() = do
    yes: Boolean = (1 < 2)
    no: Boolean = (2 < 1)
    none = NoReductionPair[\ZZ32\]
    some = SumReduction[\ZZ32\].distribute(MaxReduction[\ZZ32\])

    assert(yes.cond[\ZZ32\](fn (): ZZ32 => 1, fn (): ZZ32 => 2), 1, "a condition that holds runs its first branch")
    assert(no.cond[\ZZ32\](fn (): ZZ32 => 1, fn (): ZZ32 => 2), 2, "a condition that does not hold runs its second branch")
    assert(inOrder(yes.indexValuePairs), "(0,()),", "a condition that holds pairs its one element with index 0")
    assert(inOrder(no.indexValuePairs), "", "a condition that does not hold has no index-value pairs")
    assert(inOrder(none.indexValuePairs), "", "the empty reduction pair has no index-value pairs")
    assert(yes.ivmap[\ZZ32\](fn (i: ZZ32, u: ()): ZZ32 => i + 7).asString, "Just(7)", "a condition that holds, mapped with its index 0 by adding 7, is Just(7)")
    assert(no.ivmap[\ZZ32\](fn (i: ZZ32, u: ()): ZZ32 => i + 7).asString, "Nothing", "a condition that does not hold, mapped with its index, is Nothing")
    assert(none.ivmap[\ZZ32\](fn (i: ZZ32, p: Any): ZZ32 => 5).asString, "Nothing", "the empty reduction pair mapped with its index is Nothing")
    assert(some.ivmap[\ZZ32\](fn (i: ZZ32, p: Any): ZZ32 => i + 5).asString, "Just(5)", "a reduction pair mapped with its index 0 by adding 5 is Just(5)")
    assert(none.map[\ZZ32\](fn (p: Any): ZZ32 => 5).asString, "Nothing", "the empty reduction pair mapped is Nothing")
    assert(some.map[\ZZ32\](fn (p: Any): ZZ32 => 5).asString, "Just(5)", "a reduction pair mapped to 5 is Just(5)")

    assert(some.inner.empty().asString, "Just(0)", "the sum lifted to fuse with the maximum has the identity Just(0)")
    assert(some.inner.join(Just[\ZZ32\](2), Just[\ZZ32\](3)).asString, "Just(5)", "the sum lifted to fuse with the maximum joins Just(2) and Just(3) to Just(5)")
    assert(MinReduction[\ZZ32\].simpleJoin(3, 2), 2, "the minimum reduction joins 3 and 2 to 2")
    assert(NewlineReduction.simpleJoin("x", "y"), "x" // "y", "the newline reduction joins two strings with a newline between them")
    mi = MIMapReduceReduction[\ZZ32\](fn (a, b) => a + b, 0)
    assert(mi.empty(), 0, "a map-reduce reduction's identity is the identity it was given")
    assert(mi.join(2, 3), 5, "a map-reduce reduction joins with the function it was given")

    assert(__whileCond(Just[\ZZ32\](5), fn (e: ZZ32): () => ()), true, "a while condition over Just(5) answers true")
    assert(__whileCond(Nothing[\ZZ32\], fn (e: ZZ32): () => ()), false, "a while condition over Nothing answers false")
    n: ZZ32 := 3
    total: ZZ32 := 0
    while v <- (if n > 0 then Just[\ZZ32\](n) else Nothing[\ZZ32\] end) do
        total += v
        n -= 1
    end
    assert(total, 6, "a while loop binding 3, 2 and 1 from a condition sums them to 6")

    assert(BIG MIN <|[\ZZ32\] 4, 2, 7 |>, 2, "the minimum of 4, 2 and 7 is 2")

assert(BIG MIN <|[\ZZ32\] 4, 2, 7 |>, 2, "the minimum of 4, 2 and 7 is 2")
    assert(BIG MINNUM <|[\RR64\] 2.5, 1.5 |>, 1.5, "the floating minimum of 2.5 and 1.5 is 1.5")
    assert(BIG MAXNUM <|[\RR64\] 2.5, 1.5 |>, 2.5, "the floating maximum of 2.5 and 1.5 is 2.5")
    assert(BIG AND <|[\Boolean\] yes, no |>, false, "the conjunction of true and false is false")
    assert(BIG || <|[\ZZ32\] 1, 2 |>, "12", "the concatenation of 1 and 2 is 12")
    assert(BIG // <|[\String\] "a", "b" |>, "a" // "b", "the newline concatenation of a and b is a, a newline and b")
    assert((BIG SQCAP <|[\UniqueItem[\ZZ32\]\] Just[\ZZ32\](2), Just[\ZZ32\](2) |>).asString, "Just(2)", "the meet of Just(2) and Just(2) is Just(2)")
    assert((BIG SQCUP <|[\UniqueItem[\ZZ32\]\] Just[\ZZ32\](2), Just[\ZZ32\](3) |>).asString, "NotUnique", "the join of Just(2) and Just(3) is NotUnique")

    l = <|[\ZZ32\] 1, 3, 2 |>
    increasing = relationalPredicate[\ZZ32\](fn (a: ZZ32, b: ZZ32): Boolean => a < b)
    assert(increasing(l).holds, false, "1, 3, 2 is not increasing")
    assert(increasing(<|[\ZZ32\] 1, 2 |>).holds, true, "1, 2 is increasing")
    assert(inOrder((inits l).filter(increasing).seed), "1,3,2,", "a filtered generator of generators keeps the seed of the one it filters")
    assert(fusedMax(inits l), 6, "the maximum prefix sum of 1, 3, 2 is 6")
    assert(fusedMax((inits l).filter(increasing)), 4, "the maximum sum of the increasing prefixes of 1, 3, 2 is 4")
    assert(naiveMax(inits l), 6, "the maximum prefix sum of 1, 3, 2 without fusion is 6")
    assert(naiveMax((inits l).filter(increasing)), 4, "the maximum sum of the increasing prefixes of 1, 3, 2 without fusion is 4")
    assert(fusedMax(<|[\Generator[\ZZ32\]\] <|[\ZZ32\] 1, 2 |>, <|[\ZZ32\] 5 |> |>), 5, "the maximum of the sums of 1, 2 and of 5 is 5")

    assert(inOrder(yes.nest[\ZZ32\](fn (u: ()): Generator[\ZZ32\] => 0#3)), "0,1,2,", "a condition that holds, nested, generates the inner generator")
    assert(inOrder(no.nest[\ZZ32\](fn (u: ()): Generator[\ZZ32\] => 0#3)), "", "a condition that does not hold, nested, generates nothing")
    assert(inOrder(some.nest[\ZZ32\](fn (p: Any): Generator[\ZZ32\] => 0#2)), "0,1,", "a reduction pair, nested, generates the inner generator")
    assert(inOrder(none.nest[\ZZ32\](fn (p: Any): Generator[\ZZ32\] => 0#2)), "", "the empty reduction pair, nested, generates nothing")
    assert(yes[0#1].holds, true, "a condition that holds, indexed by its one index, is still a condition that holds")
    assert(yes[0#0].holds, false, "a condition that holds, indexed by an empty range, holds no element")
    assert(no[0#0].holds, false, "a condition that does not hold, indexed by an empty range, holds no element")
    assert(inOrder(none.cross[\ZZ32\](0#2)), "", "the empty reduction pair crossed with a generator generates nothing")
    assert(SUM[\ZZ32\][(p, k) <- some.cross[\ZZ32\](10#2)] k, 21, "a reduction pair crossed with 10 and 11 pairs itself with each of them")
    mapped = (0#5).map[\ZZ32\](fn (x: ZZ32): ZZ32 => 10 x)
    assert(inOrder(mapped[1#3].ivmap[\ZZ32\](fn (i: ZZ32, e: ZZ32): ZZ32 => i + e)), "10,21,32,", "a mapped indexed generator's slice, mapped with its indices from 0, adds each index to 10, 20 and 30")
    nested = (0#3).nest[\ZZ32\](fn (i: ZZ32): Generator[\ZZ32\] => (10 i)#2)
    assert(inOrder(nested.reverse), "21,20,11,10,1,0,", "a nested generator reversed generates the inner elements back to front")
    assert(|((inits l).filter(increasing)).theorems[\ZZ32, AnyMaybe, ZZ32\]()|, 1, "a filtered generator of generators answers the one theorem of the generator it filters")
end

end

(* Under walk, a pair is not below a tuple type over a self-bounded type parameter that nothing fixed when overloads are compared, so the overload over Any runs, while a lone method over the tuple type runs for the pair. *)

object Holder[\T extends StandardTotalOrder[\T\]\]()
    pick(x: (T,T)): String = "tuple"
    pick(x: Any): String = "any"
    one(x: (T,T)): String = "one"

    println("PASS")
  end

show N [--short]           row N under its section and table header; with
                             --short, its status, class, claim and the notes'
                             first 300 characters
  find WORDS [--open] [--cites FILE[:LINE]] [--all]
                             one line per row that holds every word (whole
                             words, or a word's start with a trailing *):
                             number, status, class, the claim's start; --open
                             leaves out FIXED, DUPLICATE and RETIRED; --cites
                             keeps the rows citing FILE (at LINE) and prints
                             the lines they cite; at most 10 rows unless --all
  count                      the rows by status, kind and area; nothing stored
  add FILE --section TITLE   FILE holds one row line, its # cell `?` (or the
                             seven cells after it); numbers it max + 1 and
                             inserts it in that section's table in number
                             order
  note N TEXT                appends TEXT to row N's notes
  close N --commit HASH --test NAME [--note TEXT] [--claim C] [--class C]
        [--spec C] [--found-by C]
                             after the fix has landed: HASH must be in HEAD's
                             history and NAME a test under the test folders;
                             writes the one-line FIXED row (the claim's first
                             sentence, the test as reproducer, notes `fixed
                             HASH; full text: history, row N`); the options
                             give cells the old row lacks in the template's form
  duplicate N --of M [--add TEXT] [--claim C] [--class C] [--spec C]
        [--reproducer C] [--found-by C]
                             makes row N a DUPLICATE pointer to row M (notes
                             `duplicate of row M; full text: history, row N`);
                             --add appends TEXT to row M's notes
  check [--rows FILE] [--base COMMIT] [--summary]
                             lints every row against the template, and the
                             tables' headers, numbers and order; --rows lints
                             a file holding only row lines instead; --base
                             also checks that every row at COMMIT is the same
                             line now or has its full earlier line in the
                             history file, and that the set of row numbers is
                             unchanged; --summary prints only the counts by
                             rule; exit 1 on any failure

Text given on the command line (TEXT, C) has its bare pipes escaped.

# Rung G of climb batch 12: the skeptic's verdict

The head judged is `1410a62de`, the worker's last commit on `wip/rung-reduction-types`, cut from the base `7fa767d48`. Its report and record came from the run's journal (`0b177549a`). The skeptic's commits after it are `17e5c14d9` and `dca01ad7e`, both corrections, and this file. The rung edits no Java or Scala and builds nothing, so no fix here was built and no suite ran. The count and distance tables the report quotes are those of the worker's head; the gate's tables on the merged tree are the record.

Verdict: **approved**. The change is right and as small as its section asks. The record had three false or missing items, now corrected on the branch. No fix is contested.

## 1. What was checked, and what holds

- **The stage, the rung's failing-then-passing test.** `explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/compare.sh explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-11/gate/distance.txt tmp/rung-reduction-types/distance-postedit.txt` prints `DISTANCE DOWN   207 -> 194 (-13)`, `kind abstract-method 8 -> 0 (-8)`, `kind typecheck 156 -> 151 (-5)`. Grouped by kind, unit and location against `explorations/compile-ladder/gate/distance-sites.tsv` (a script of the skeptic's own), 13 sites are gone: abstract-method at `FortressLibrary.fss:3289`, `:3298`, `:3307`, `:3338`, `:3358`, `:3378`, `:3398`, `:3496`, and typecheck at `:3107`, `:3119`, `:3133`, `:3144`, `:3162`. No site came. Five changed only their message, as the report's section 3 says: row 433's two return-type sites, row 425's two `BIG MIN` sites and the export site `:12`. The count's `diff` against `climb-batch-11/gate/checker-count.txt` is empty. The worker ran the count at 11:07:52 and the distance at 11:11:22, after its last edit of code at 11:07:24, and the distance tools changed between the landed gate and the base (`git diff --name-only f9d3ec826 7fa767d48 -- explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/` lists `classify.py`, `run.sh`, `table.py`, `test_classify.py`). So the report reads the sites by row and kind, not by class, and is right to.
- **Test first.** In the worker's transcript, the tests `UnwrittenBigMinMaxWalk.fss` (promoted by `git mv`) and `UnwrittenTupleMinMaxWalk.fss` were written at 10:56:21 to 10:56:39. They failed through the harness on the base's code at 10:56:46 (call `EF61Bu`: `# harness-one 2026-10-09T10:56:46Z; tree 7fa767d48`, `** bug! MethodClosure simpleJoin(a:Any,b:Any):Any... has neither body nor def`, `Tests run: 3,  Failures: 3`). The guard `UnwrittenBigOperatorsWalk.fss` passed on the base at 10:57:21 (`4FNPyu`: `PASS`, `OK (1 test)`). The first library edit was at 10:58:42 (`bg7aUS`). The last change of code, the demo's line, was at 11:07:24. `ant testSystem` started after it, at 11:07:29 (`FFbtXo`), and ended `BUILD SUCCESSFUL` with shards 129, 133, 132 and 135, which is 529 tests and 0 failures (`tzrMoC`, `ueeaaR`). The expected failure `XXXUnwrittenSetBigOperatorsWalk.fss` was shown both ways (`raMvWB`: `OK Saw expected exception`, and with the static arguments written, `Missing expected failure`, `Tests run: 1,  Failures: 1`).
- **The diff, line by line.** Every changed library line types one of row 628's three devices, or follows the lifted type where it changed. The changes are:
  - `AssociativeReduction` and `LiftedCommutativeMonoidReduction` at `Maybe[\R\]`, with `simpleJoin(a:R, b:R): R` and `lift(r:R)`;
  - `MonoidReduction`'s `lift(r:R)`;
  - the identity-less big operators and their sugar, and `Set`'s `BIG INTERSECTION`;
  - P2's three completing edits: `ActualReduction`'s abstract `lift(r: R): L`, as `.fsi:1869` declares it; `Just[\R\]` in the lifted bodies, as `:3105` writes `Nothing[\R\]`; and `MinReduction`'s and `MaxReduction`'s `simpleJoin(a:T, b:T): T`, as `.fsi:1979` and `:1987` declare them;
  - the fusion pairs and `distribute` at `Maybe[\T\]`, which row 628's section allows ("it follows the lifted type's spelling where that type changes");
  - `Generator22D.fss:207`, at `Maybe[\SomeMSS2DTuple[\R\]\]`, the lifted type of `MSS2DReductionAbove[\R\]` (an `AssociativeReduction[\SomeMSS2DTuple[\T\]\]`, `Library/Generator22D.fss:377`).

  No declaration of R's ranges section, of S's numbers, arrays and strings sections, of `SUFFIX_SUM` (`:4684`) or of the identities is touched. The api lines match the component's. `AnyMaybe` remains only in its own declarations and in `QuickCheck.fss:758`'s `typecase`.
- **The library's way.** The api's `lift(r:R)` and `simpleJoin(a:T, b:T): T`, `Set`'s `Intersection` at `Maybe[\Set[\E\]\]`, and the library's 31 `Just[\` spellings are the precedents. No `lift(r: Any)`, bare lifted `Just(...)` or `AnyMaybe` lifted type is left in `Library/` or `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/` (grep). The two `Any` devices left in the section are `ActualReduction`'s `distribute(r: Any)` and `MIMapReduceReduction` with `embiggen` (row 631), as the report says. The top-level `CompilerLibrary/FortressLibrary.fsi:1766-1771` and `CompilerLibrary/Set.fsi:65` keep the old devices. They are the team's `.fsi` stubs, which no source path reads (`git log -- CompilerLibrary/` stops at the cut `5a68404fd`), so they are not sibling sites.
- **The tests.** Each test file has one comment line and is named by its topic. Each message cites `reductions.tex`, section "Summations and Other Reduction Expressions", whose sentence "The resulting values are combined together using *Op*" (`Specification/basic/expressions/reductions.tex:76-79`) is what the messages say. `UnwrittenBigMinMaxWalk.fss` did the same when it was batch 11's. No test name collides: a search of `ProjectFortress/tests`, `compiler_tests`, `library_tests`, `other_compiler_tests`, `test_library`, `Library` and `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress` finds each name in its own file only.

Each says what the report says. The precedent `CLIMB-BATCH-6.md:193` is the demo respelled after its test twin. The team's port `ProjectFortress/BirdyLib/Util.fsi:26-32` is Tristan King's `98f797296`.
- **record.md.** The new rows were linted with `ledger.py check --rows` on a numbered copy: NEW-G-1 and NEW-G-2 each give `0 fail the template`. The FACTS entry, the notes and the revival-change entry are true as written, but for the FACTS correction amended below (finding 3). `revival-changes.md` has no heading between "Numbers are siblings, not a tower" and "Specified, but not built", so the new heading's place is right.

## 2. The skeptic's own programs: old code against new

The programs are under `tmp/rung-reduction-types/skeptic/` and are not committed. Old code: `/home/user/fortress-base12/explorations/coordinator/tools/old-fortress.sh /home/user/fortress-base12 /home/user/fortress-reductions/tmp/old-caches P.fss`. New code: `bin/fortress P.fss` in the rung's tree. Walk ran at `FORTRESS_THREADS=1` unless the table says otherwise. The diff has no mutable variable, field, atomic block or write into a library's state, so threads were varied only as a check.

|---|---|---|
